post.summary: Snapshot every table of a database dataset again (admin only)
post.description: Copies every table this database dataset holds: tables snapshotted before and tables kept as metadata only, never tables the admin left unticked. One read-only REPEATABLE READ transaction, so all tables show the same moment; then every declared foreign key between held tables is recorded as a relation. A table whose content did not change gets no new version (`created: false`); the status is 200 when no table changed. No table count limit: a table over SOURCE_MAX_ROWS, or that would take the snapshot over SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_MAX_MB (Postgres sizes, smallest tables first), keeps metadata only (`metadata_only`); MAX_UPLOAD_MB applies to each copied table. A table the account can no longer read is skipped and listed in `unreadable`. SOURCE_RESNAPSHOT_HOURS runs the same on a schedule.

query_id.description: `AskResponse.query_id` (or `TurnItem.query_id`) of an answered question the caller asked.

AnswerVerdict.description:
Verdict of the two checks on a text written by the language model: `match` (agrees with the computed numbers),
`warning` (some parts can be read several ways, not certainly wrong), `mismatch` (wrong on every attempt; the model's
text is replaced by a template sentence).

choices.description:
Choices for the question, empty the first time. To change an assumption or answer a clarification, send the
same question with `choices` of the previous answer, the changed entry replaced or added. A question whose text
was edited is a new question: send `choices` empty. The backend does not compare with earlier questions; it
applies the choices it recognizes for this question and ignores the others with a warning
`choice_not_applied`. Choices not listed use their default.

conversation_id.description:
Conversation to continue, from `AskResponse.conversation_id` of the previous question; the model then reads the
question as a follow-up of the last turns. Leave out to start a new conversation. A conversation of another
user or another dataset is 404.

AskResponse.description: Answer to one question, with the evidence behind it. See `AskStatus` for which fields are set.

answer_text.description:
Short answer in Vietnamese for an `answered` question that is not a "why" question and has at least one row:
`insight.summary` when the language model wrote it and it passed the checks (the model only sees the sentences
the backend computed, never result rows), otherwise a template sentence written by the backend. A list of rows
without aggregates always gets the template (row count and filters). Null otherwise; a "why" question has
`explanation.summary`.

answer_text_by_model.description:
True when `answer_text` is the language model's text of `insight.summary`, false for the template sentence (no
checked model text, a list of rows, or `ANSWER_TEXT=false`). Null when `answer_text` is null.

choices.description:
Every choice this answer used, defaults included, in the shape of `AskRequest.choices`. To ask again with one
choice changed, send this list with that entry replaced; for `needs_choice`, send it plus a pick for each
clarification. Choices the backend did not recognize are not in it.

clarifications.description: Questions back to the user, only for `needs_choice`. Every entry has `selected` null.

conversation_id.description:
Conversation this question belongs to (`AskRequest.conversation_id`, or a new one when it was empty). Send it
back with the next question so the model reads it as a follow-up.

oneOf.description:
Dates the data covers for the time column the answer relies on: the first column of the table's time columns that
the SQL that ran names, otherwise the table's first time column. Read from the column profile of the whole table
(a user limited to some rows still sees the range of the whole table). Null for a question that is not
`answered`, or when the table has no usable time column.

Breakdown of a "why" question; for other answered questions, the automatic breakdown behind `insight` when it
has one (the change of a single number against the period before, or the period of a time series that changed
most). Null otherwise.

What the result says, for an `answered` question that is not a "why" question and has at least one row with a
value: chosen by the shape of the result, every number computed by the backend. Null otherwise; a "why" question
has `explanation.summary`.

message.description:
Text for the end user (Vietnamese): the reason for `rejected` and `failed`, the prompt for `needs_choice`;
null for `answered`.

model.description: Language model configured for the question, for example `gemini-2.5-flash` or `mock`.

model_calls.description:
Every call to the language model for this question, in the order the calls finished, with wall time and tokens.
The sum of `duration_ms` is the time spent waiting for the model; the rest of the step time is the backend.

query_id.description: Id of the question in the history (`queries`); null for `needs_choice`.

question.description: The question exactly as sent in `AskRequest.question`.

oneOf.description: Kind of the question chosen by the classify step; null when the question stopped before that step.

sql_generated.description: SQL written by the model, on logical table names. After a fix round, the fixed SQL.

sql_guarded.description:
SQL that ran: the generated SQL after the guard added row-level filters and a row limit. Still on logical table
names, no file paths.

steps.description:
What the backend did, in order, with timings. A step may appear twice, for example `run` before and after a
`repair`.

table_id.description:
Table the question started from (the table routes `/datasets/{id}/drill` and `/conversations` take this id).
Asked on a whole dataset (`/catalog/{id}/ask`), the backend picks it; asked on a table, it is that table.

tables_read.description:
Tables `sql_guarded` read, in the order the query first reads them: the dataset asked about, and related
datasets of the same database snapshot when the SQL joins them. Empty unless the status is `answered`.

version_id.description: Version of `table_id` the question ran on.

warnings.description: Notes shown next to the result; they never hide it.

AskStatus.description:
Outcome of the question, and which fields of `AskResponse` are set:
- `answered`: the SQL ran. Set: `query_id`, `sql_generated`, `sql_guarded`, `understanding`, `result`; `chart`
  when a chart fits; `explanation` for a "why" question (when the breakdown cannot be made, a warning
  `explanation_unavailable` says why).
- `needs_choice`: the question can be read several ways; pick one option of each entry in `clarifications` and ask
  again. This can happen before the model is called (a word matches several columns) or after (the two slices of
  a "why" question cannot be told). Set: `message`, `clarifications`; `sql_generated` when the model was called.
  Not recorded in the history, so `query_id` is null.
- `rejected`: the guard refused the SQL the model wrote in the `repair` round (when the guard refuses the model's
  first SQL, for any reason, the question always gets that round), or the SQL the server built for a "why"
  breakdown. Set: `message`, `query_id`, `sql_generated`. For the model's SQL, the `guard` step that stopped it has
  `ok` false and the guard's reason in `detail`, and `message` is a fixed text asking to rephrase the question, since
  the user cannot fix the SQL; for a breakdown, `message` gives the guard's reason. Also when
  the model finds that no column of the dataset holds the information the question needs (a rating that is not
  there, a forecast): no SQL runs, `sql_generated` is null, and `message` gives the reason and the closest columns.
- `failed`: the SQL could not run and the one fix round did not help, either because the fixed SQL failed too or
  because the model failed during the fix; or the SQL ran past the time or memory limit, which gets no fix round.
  Set: `message`, `query_id`, `sql_generated`; `sql_guarded` unless that SQL never passed the guard. The `run` or
  `repair` step that stopped it has `ok` false.

A fix round starts when the analytics engine fails on the SQL, when the guard refuses it for any reason, or when the
model's reply cannot be read; there is at most one round per question, and the fixed SQL goes through the guard
again. The status names the step that stopped the question: the guard gives `rejected`, the engine or the fix round
gives `failed`. A model error before any SQL exists is not a status: the request gets 502 or 503.

detail.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese), for example the guard's reason or the engine error.

ok.description:
False for a step that failed. A failed step does not always stop the question: a failed `run` or `guard` can be
followed by `repair`, a failed `narrate` by a template summary. `AskStatus` tells whether the question stopped.

email.description: Email of an active account; it becomes `admin` of the workspace.

AutoReportResponse.description: The automatic report just built, and the sections that could not be built.

skipped.description: One Vietnamese sentence per planned section left out, with the reason.

BreakdownKey.description: One group of a breakdown table in one slice.

column.description: `DimensionBreakdown.column`: a column name of the dataset, not of `result.columns`.

oneOf.description: `GroupContribution.value` of the group; null for the group of empty cells.

Calculation.description: A common way to compute the concept, in words, not tied to the columns of a dataset.

description.description: What it computes and when to pick it over the others.

CellValue.description: One cell: a JSON number, string or boolean; read it with the `kind` of its column.

ChartKind.description:
Kind of chart:
- `bar`: horizontal bars, one per group of `x`, largest first; compares groups.
- `column`: vertical columns over the periods of `x`; up to 10 periods.
- `line`: a line with a marker on each period of `x`; more than 10 periods, or one line per group of `series`.
- `stacked_column`: vertical columns over the periods of `x`, each split into the groups of `series`.

ChartLayout.description:
How the measures in `y` are drawn:
- `single`: one measure.
- `grouped`: side by side on one scale, because the measures share a unit.
- `panels`: one small chart per measure sharing the axis of `x`, because the units differ or are unknown; two
  scales in one chart are not used, since choosing them can make the same numbers look like anything.

ChartSuggestion.description:
Suggested chart; null in `AskResponse` when the result is better shown as a table only (one value, too many
groups, more than one grouping column without time). Every name is a name from `result.columns`.

other_bucket.description:
The groups after `top` can be summed into one entry labelled "Khác": every measure is a sum or a plain count,
and `result` holds every row. False: they are left out, and the chart says how many.

ratio.description:
Measures in `y` that are not totals (averages, ratios, minimum, maximum): drawn as narrow columns, and never
summed into a "Khác" entry.

series.description:
For `stacked_column`, and for `line` with one line per group: the group column whose values become the parts
or the lines. Null otherwise.

top.description: Most groups to draw, largest first: bars for `bar`, parts for `stacked_column`. Null when every group is drawn.

x.description: Category axis: a group column for `bar`, a time column for the other kinds.

Choice.description:
A point where the question can be read several ways. To change it, ask the same question again with
`AskResponse.choices`, the entry for this `id` replaced.

label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese): what can be read several ways, for example which column a word means.

selected.description: Id of the option in use; null when the user has to pick (`needs_choice`).

id.description: Opaque id set by the backend; send it back unchanged.

ChosenOption.description:
The pick for one `Choice`. A `choice_id` or `option_id` the backend does not recognize (for example a choice that
no longer applies) is ignored, left out of `AskResponse.choices`, and reported with a warning `choice_not_applied`:
an assumption falls back to its default, a clarification is asked again.

option_id.description: One of the `ChoiceOption.id` of that choice.

ColumnAggregation.description:
How the values of a measure column are combined when no metric says otherwise: `sum` for amounts and quantities,
`avg` for values that describe one row (age, score, credits, days).

ColumnAggregationRequest.description: New default aggregation of one measure column of the current version.

ColumnRole.description:
What a result column is:
- `dimension`: a grouping key that is not time, for example a market.
- `time`: a grouping key on time, for example a quarter.
- `measure`: an aggregate, for example a sum; its cells can be drilled into.
- `other`: anything else, for example a column of a query without aggregates.

Comparison.description:
- `periods`: the slices are two periods; `compare` is the later one.
- `groups`: the slices are two values of one column, with no order in time.

id.description: Dataset id. For a database, the same id as its source in `/sources/{id}` (admin only).

metadata_only.description:
Tables of the database kept with columns, types, keys and comments but no rows (over SOURCE_MAX_ROWS or the
SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_MAX_MB total), ordered by `table`. An admin snapshots one with `POST /sources/{id}/snapshot`
and `tables: [table]`. Empty for a file.

name.description: Database name for a database, the name given at upload for a file.

relations.description: Foreign-key relations between tables of this dataset, copied from the source database. Empty for a file.

tables.description:
Tables, ordered by `source_table` (schema, then table) and then by name. A file has one table; a database
connected but not snapshotted yet has none.

updated_at.description: Latest `current_version_at` of its tables: the last snapshot or upload. Null while no table has data.

DatasetTable.description:
A table of a dataset. Its id is the id the table routes take: `/datasets/{id}/overview`, `/metrics`, `/drill`,
`/conversations/{conversation_id}`.

columns.description: Columns of the current version, in table order; empty without a current version.

current_profile_status.description:
`pending`, `structure`, `semantic` or `failed`; null without a current version. Asking works from
`structure` on.

current_version_at.description: When the current version was created: upload time, or the last snapshot.

description.description: Table comment from the source database (`COMMENT ON TABLE`) at the current version; null when none.

logical_table.description: Table name used in SQL; unique within the dataset only, so two databases can both have `orders`.

row_count.description: Rows in the current version; null while the table has no data.

schema.description: Schema in the source database (`sales` for `sales.orders`); null for a file.

source_table.description: `schema.table` in the source database; null for a file.

suggested_questions.description: Suggested questions of the current version; empty until the semantic profile is done.

description.description:
Description of the snapshotted table written in the source database (`COMMENT ON TABLE`); null for uploaded
files and tables without a comment.

DimensionBreakdown.description: Contribution of every group of one dimension; the contributions add up to `change`.

column.description: Dimension column, as named in the dataset (not a name from `result.columns`).

groups.description: Every group of the column, largest contribution (by absolute value) first.

has_outliers.description:
True when at least one group is an `outlier`. Dimensions with outliers come first, each part in the order of
how well the dimension explains the change.

kind.description: How to read the group values, like the `kind` of a result column.

label.description: Vietnamese name of the column from the column profile; null when the profile has none.

mix_effect.description: Ratio measures only: sum of `mix_effect` of every group; `mix_effect + rate_effect` is `change`.

rate_effect.description: Ratio measures only: sum of `rate_effect` of every group.

sql.description: SQL that computed the groups of both slices, after the guard.

DrillKey.description: One grouping key of the clicked cell.

column.description: A name from `result.columns`, of a column with role `dimension` or `time`.

oneOf.description: The cell of that column in the clicked row, exactly as received; null for a SQL NULL.

DrillMeasure.description: One measure of the clicked number, computed again over its source rows.

column.description:
Name of the measure column in the answer's `result.columns` (for a breakdown row, the column of the clicked
slice in the breakdown query).

row_column.description:
With rule `sum`: the column of `result` that holds each row's part, so the rows of all pages add up to
`value`. null otherwise.

oneOf.description:
The aggregate of the answer over every source row of the number. Equal to the clicked cell when the member
clicking sees the same rows as the member who asked.

DrillRequest.description:
Which number to trace back to its source rows: set exactly one of `cell` and `breakdown`. Rows come one page at a
time, sorted by every column of the page, so pages do not overlap.

oneOf.description: A row of the breakdown in `AskResponse.explanation`: the source rows of that group in that slice.

cell.description:
A cell of `AskResponse.result`: the values of every `dimension` and `time` column of its row, one key per
column. An empty list is the one row of a query without grouping keys.

offset.description: Number of source rows to skip. Default 0.

query_id.description: `AskResponse.query_id` of the answer the number belongs to.

DrillResponse.description: One page of the source rows behind a number.

joined_columns.description:
Columns of `result` that come from the joined tables rather than from `source_table`: the grouping keys and
filter columns of the question on those tables. Empty when the question reads one table.

measures.description:
The measures of the clicked number, each computed again over all source rows (every page). For a breakdown row,
only the measure of the clicked slice.

result.description:
The page. For a question on one table: every column of the dataset, including `_source_file`, the file each
row came from. For a question that joins tables: every column of `source_table`, then `joined_columns`. Then,
for each `sum` measure over an expression rather than one column of the page, its `row_column`. Here `result.total_rows` counts the rows of this page only.

source_table.description:
The data table the rows come from. For a question that joins tables, this is the table the measures add up
(the many side, such as `order_items` joined to `orders` and `customers`): one row of `result` per row of it
that went into the number, its columns first. null when the rows come from a WITH table or a subquery that
does not start from a data table.

sql.description:
The SQL that read this page, after the guard: the filters of the answered question, the keys of the clicked
number, and the row filters of the member asking now (which may differ from the member who asked the question).

total_rows.description: Number of source rows behind the number, over all pages.

DropReason.description:
- `separates_slices`: every value of the column is found in one slice only, so the column only renames the two
  slices.
- `duplicates`: the column splits the rows into exactly the groups of another column (`duplicate_of`).

DroppedDimension.description: One dimension left out, and why.

base_only.description: For `separates_slices`: values found only in the base slice, as text.

compare_only.description: For `separates_slices`: values found only in the compared slice, as text.

duplicate_of.description: Column with the same groups, for `duplicates`.

label.description: Vietnamese name of the column from the column profile; null when the profile has none.

ErrorBody.description: Error body returned by every endpoint on failure.

field.description: Name of the request field the error is about, when it is about one field. Omitted otherwise.

message.description: Human-readable explanation in Vietnamese, meant to be shown to the end user as is.

ErrorCode.description: Stable machine-readable error code; one per HTTP status.

ErrorEntry.description: One row of the error log.

model_output.description: What the model returned at that step: SQL, the form as JSON, or the text it wrote.

query_id.description: The recorded question; null when it was not recorded (waiting for a choice) or was deleted.

ErrorStep.description: The step where the model went wrong.

EvalCaseCandidate.description:
One approved example as a candidate case for the evaluation set, in the format of the files in `eval/` (for
example `eval/dataco.json`). Review each case before adding it: check the SQL and set `ordered`.

ordered.description: Always false here; set it to true when the row order is part of the answer (top N, time series).

ExampleCandidate.description: An answer rated `good`, for admins to review as an example question.

approved_at.description: Null until an admin approves it as an example question.

dataset_id.description: Null when the dataset was deleted.

rated_by.description: Name or email of who rated it; null when the account was deleted.

row_count.description: Rows of the result when it was asked; results are not stored.

sql.description: SQL the model wrote, before the guard; for a why question, the SQL built from its form.

understood.description: Short text of the "understood as" card; null when the question was not asked in a conversation.

why.description: A why question: its example in the prompt is the form the model filled, not SQL.

Explanation.description:
Breakdown of a change between two slices (two periods or two groups); see `AskResponse.explanation` for when it is
set. Numbers are exact strings of decimal digits.

comparison.description:
What the two slices are, which decides the words for the change: up or down between two periods, higher or
lower between two groups.

counts_rows.description: True when the measure counts rows (a count, not a sum): the measure is then itself the size of each slice.

dimensions.description: One breakdown per dimension, the dimension that explains the change best first.

dropped_dimensions.description:
Dimensions left out of `dimensions` or of the summary, with the reason; show them as a note with the
breakdown so that a missing table is explained.

measure.description: Measure that changed, text for the end user (Vietnamese).

measure_kind.description: How the measure adds up over groups, which decides how to read the numbers below.

percent_change.description: `change / base.value * 100`, rounded to one decimal; null when `base.value` is zero or negative.

slice_column.description: Column whose two values are compared, for `groups`; null for `periods`.

slice_column_label.description: Vietnamese name of `slice_column` from the column profile; null when the profile has none.

summary.description:
Plain-language summary for the end user (Vietnamese), as one text: `summary_title` then each point as
"lead: text". When `summary_by_model` the model wrote it from the numbers the backend computed, its claims were
checked against this breakdown and an independent model call compared the meaning of the text with the claims
and the names of the two slices; otherwise the backend wrote it from a template.

summary_by_model.description:
False when `summary` is a template sentence written by the backend: the change is zero (the model is not
called), the model was not reached, the independent check could not judge the text, or
the text failed the checks twice (one rewrite is asked).

summary_points.description:
Points under the main answer (Vietnamese). When `summary_by_model`, the main causes the model wrote, all of kind
`reason`; otherwise written by the backend, each said only when the numbers support it.

summary_title.description:
Main answer, one sentence (Vietnamese): written by the model when `summary_by_model`, otherwise by the backend
from the numbers above.

oneOf.description:
Outcome of the two checks on the model's text: `match` or `warning` when `summary` is the model's text,
`mismatch` when the model's text failed every attempt and `summary` is the template, null when no check ran (no
change to explain, or the model or the checking model failed).

summary_warnings.description:
Parts of the model's text that the independent check found unclear but not certainly wrong, one Vietnamese
sentence each, written by the checking model; show them with `summary`. Empty when nothing was unclear or
`summary` is a template sentence.

filter.description: SQL condition that selects the rows of the slice, on logical names.

label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese) naming the slice, for example a quarter.

rows.description: Number of rows of the slice.

value.description: Value of the measure on the slice.

FeedbackRequest.description: Rating of one answer by the member who asked it. Sending a new rating replaces the old one.

note.description: Optional short note, only with `bad`, at most 500 characters.

oneOf.description: Only with `bad`; may be left out.

FilterColumnResponse.description: A column a row rule can use: a dimension column of the table's current version.

label.description: Vietnamese label: the first alias written by the semantic profile; null until then.

values.description:
Known values of the column from its profile, most rows first; empty for a sensitive column or one with too
many values to list. A rule may still use other values.

GroupContribution.description: One group of a dimension. `value` is null for the group of rows where the dimension column is null.

contribution.description:
Part of `change` from this group: `compare_value - base_value` for a total, `mix_effect + rate_effect` for a
ratio.

mix_effect.description:
Ratio measures only: part of `change` because this group's share of the denominator changed,
`(compare_share - base_share) * (base_value + compare_value) / 2`. For a group with no denominator in one slice,
the ratio of that slice is taken equal to the other slice, so the whole contribution is a mix effect.

outlier.description:
True when the group stands out: its `share_of_change` is at least 1 (in absolute value) and its
`percent_change` is at least 10 points away from the `percent_change` of the whole, or it is `new`, `gone` or a
`sign_flip`.

percent_change.description:
`(compare_value - base_value) / base_value * 100`, one decimal. Null when the group is `new` or `gone`, when
`base_value` is zero or negative, or when `sign_flip`.

rate_effect.description:
Ratio measures only: part of `change` because the ratio inside this group changed,
`(base_share + compare_share) / 2 * (compare_value - base_value)`.

share_of_change.description:
`contribution / change * 100`, one decimal: negative when the group moved against the change, above 100 when
other groups offset it. Null when the change is close to zero (under 0.5% of the larger slice), where these
percents grow without meaning.

sign_flip.description:
True when the base and compared values are both non-zero with opposite signs, for example a profit that
turned into a loss.

oneOf.description: Value of the dimension column for this group; null for rows where it is null.

GroupPresence.description:
Where a group has rows: `both` slices, only the compared slice (`new`), or only the base slice (`gone`). For a
ratio, a group has rows in a slice when its denominator there is not zero.

Insight.description: Explanation of a plain answer, chosen by the shape of the result.

notable.description:
False when the numbers show nothing notable: a change below the threshold, too few rows to conclude, groups of
about the same size, or a plain list of rows.

points.description: Points under the main finding, written by the backend (Vietnamese).

summary.description:
Plain-language text for the end user (Vietnamese): the language model's wording of `title` and `points` when it
passed the checks, otherwise `title` and `points` joined.

summary_by_model.description:
True when `summary` was written by the language model; false when it is the backend's text (the model failed,
timed out, its text failed the checks on every attempt, or `INSIGHT_TEXT=false`). The checks: every number and
direction must come from the points, no causal word, then a separate model call compares the meaning of the text
with `title` and `points`; when a check fails or finds an unclear point, the model rewrites once.

oneOf.description:
Outcome of the two checks on the model's text: `match` or `warning` when `summary` is the model's text,
`mismatch` when the model's text failed every attempt and `summary` is the backend's text, null when no check ran
(the model was not called, failed or timed out, or the checking model failed).

summary_warnings.description:
Parts of `summary` that the separate check found unclear but not certainly wrong, one Vietnamese sentence each,
written by the checking model; show them with `summary`. Empty when nothing was unclear or `summary` is the
backend's text.

title.description: Main finding, one sentence written by the backend (Vietnamese).

InsightKind.description:
- `single_value`: one number; compared with the period before when the question names a period.
- `time_series`: one measure over periods; overall direction and the period that changed most against the one
  before, broken down by dimension in `AskResponse.explanation`.
- `groups`: one measure over the groups of one column; share of the top group, how many groups make 80% of the
  total, groups far from the mean (for a measure that does not add up, such as an average or a rate: the highest
  and the lowest group). Also one measure over two columns: the top combinations and the top group of each
  column.
- `top_n`: the first groups by a measure (the SQL has a limit); their share of the total and the gap between the
  first two.
- `rows`: anything else, such as rows without aggregates; only the number of rows and the filters.

InsightPoint.description: One point of an insight: a short lead (shown in bold) and the sentence after it.

lead.description: Lead of the point (Vietnamese), for example the words for "concentration".

Lesson.description: A short lesson for the model, written by an admin.

approved_by.description: Who last enabled it; null for a draft never enabled.

dataset_id.description: Null for a lesson of the whole workspace.

enabled.description: Approved and in use: only these lessons go into prompts.

error_id.description: The error log row it was written from.

LessonRequest.description: A new lesson, saved as a draft that is not used until enabled.

dataset_id.description: Leave out for a lesson of the whole workspace.

error_id.description: The error log row the lesson comes from, if any.

text.description: One or two short sentences, at most 300 characters.

LessonStateRequest.description: Turn a lesson on (approve it, recording who and when) or off.

ListSheetsRequest.description: Multipart form for listing the sheets of an Excel file. The file is not stored.

LlmCall.description: One call to the language model, in the order the calls finished.

duration_ms.description: Wall time from sending the request to reading the whole answer, in milliseconds.

input_tokens.description: Prompt tokens as counted by the provider; null when it did not say (mock, an error, a cancelled call).

ok.description: False when the provider returned an error, or when the caller stopped waiting (its own timeout).

output_tokens.description: Answer tokens as counted by the provider, thinking tokens included; null when it did not say.

LlmTask.description: What the language model was asked to do in one call.

column.description: The measure column, or null for a metric.

label.description: Metric name, or the column label (else name) of a measure column; also the measure column of the chart.

metric.description: The metric of that name, or null for a measure column.

workspaces.description: Workspaces the user belongs to, with their role in each, sorted by name.

MeasureKind.description:
- `total`: a sum or a count; group values add up to the slice value, a contribution is `compare_value - base_value`.
- `ratio`: a ratio or an average (numerator over denominator); slice and group values are ratios rounded to a fixed
  number of decimals, a contribution is `mix_effect + rate_effect`.

MeasureRule.description:
How the source rows make up a measure:
- `sum`: `SUM(x)`; `row_column` holds x of each row and `value` is their sum.
- `count`: `COUNT(*)`; each row counts one, so `value` equals `total_rows`.
- `other`: any other aggregate (AVG, COUNT DISTINCT, a ratio, a rounded sum); `value` is that aggregate over the
  rows, there is no per-row column.

MemberDataRolesRequest.description: The full set of data roles of a member; empty removes every role.

Membership.description: A workspace the user belongs to, with their role in it.

MetadataColumn.description: One column of a table kept as metadata only, read from the source catalog.

data_type.description: Postgres type as `format_type` writes it, for example `numeric(10,2)`.

description.description: `COMMENT ON COLUMN`, cleaned; null when none.

MetadataOnlyTable.description: A table of the source with columns, types, keys and comments but no rows.

dataset_id.description: Dataset of an earlier snapshot of this table, which keeps its last version; null when never snapshotted.

description.description: `COMMENT ON TABLE`, cleaned; null when none.

reason.description: Why, in Vietnamese, with the setting to change.

row_count.description: Rows estimated by Postgres, or counted when SOURCE_MAX_ROWS is set; null when Postgres has no statistics yet.

size_bytes.description: Size reported by Postgres; null for views.

Metric.description: A metric of the dataset: the version in use (the latest confirmed one).

confirmed.description: False for a draft nobody approved; the SQL prompt marks it as such.

expression.description: Aggregate SQL expression over the dataset's columns, for example `SUM("Order Item Total")`.

filter.description: Row condition applied with the expression, for example `"Order Status" <> 'CANCELED'`.

id.description: Id of this version; editing or deleting by it acts on the metric with this name.

time_column.description: Column that dates the rows for this metric.

version.description: Starts at 1; each edit adds a version and keeps the earlier ones.

MetricColumn.description: A column of the current version, for the column picker and the default aggregation of measure columns.

oneOf.description: Default aggregation; null unless the role is `measure`.

description_source.description:
Who wrote `description`: `database` (a `COMMENT ON COLUMN` of the source database) or `model` (the semantic
profile); null when there is no description.

MetricRequest.description: A metric to create, or the new version of one. Errors name the wrong field in `field`.

expression.description: One aggregate SQL expression over the dataset's columns, column names in double quotes.

name.description: Name users ask with, unique in the dataset ignoring case and accents. Cannot change when editing.

MetricsResponse.description: Metrics of a dataset and the columns of its current version.

columns.description: Columns of the current version in table order; empty while the dataset has no profiled version.

metrics.description: One entry per metric name, sorted by name.

MissingCode.description:
What is missing:
- `no_version`: the dataset has no data yet.
- `profile_pending`: the column profile is being built; no columns or charts yet.
- `profile_failed`: the profile failed; upload the file again.
- `semantic_pending`: labels, descriptions and units are being written.
- `semantic_unavailable`: the current model cannot write labels, descriptions and units.
- `restricted`: the viewer's data role filters rows, so per-column counts and value charts are left out.
- `no_time`: no time column, so no time span and no time charts.
- `no_measure`: no confirmed metric and no money or quantity measure column, so no measure chart.
- `chart_failed`: a chart query failed; the message says why.

NumberCheck.description:
Outcome of the number check (the backend compares every number and direction of the model's text with the computed
facts): `passed` (the shown text is the model's and passed), `replaced` (the model's text failed and the shown text
was written by the backend), `not_needed` (the backend wrote the text from the numbers, no model text to check).

column.description: Column of the profile the chart is about: the dimension for `rows_by_value`, the time column otherwise.

oneOf.description: Null for `rows_by_value`.

sql.description: SQL after the guard that computed the chart; null for `rows_by_value`, which no query computes.

OverviewChartKind.description:
Kind of pre-built chart:
- `measure_over_time`: the main measure by day or month.
- `rows_over_time`: number of rows by day or month, to see periods with little data or data that stops mid-period.
- `rows_by_value`: number of rows for each value of a dimension column, read from the profile.

description_source.description:
Who wrote `description`: `database` (a `COMMENT ON COLUMN` of the source database) or `model` (the semantic
profile); null when there is no description.

distinct_count.description: Exact number of different values; null when `summary.restricted`.

label.description: Vietnamese label: the first alias written by the semantic profile; null until then.

null_percent.description: Share of empty cells, 0 to 100; null when `summary.restricted`.

sensitive.description: Marked sensitive: no values are returned for it.

unit.description: money, quantity, percent, duration or other; null when unknown.

values.description: Values with their row counts, most rows first; only for dimension columns that are not sensitive, at most 200.

confirmed.description: False while an admin has not confirmed the definition.

expression.description: Aggregate over the columns, for example `SUM("Order Item Total")`.

OverviewRole.description: Role of a column in the profile; the rules are in docs/DATA.md.

restricted.description:
True when the viewer's data role filters rows. Per-column counts and value frequencies are computed on every
row, so they are left out: null `null_percent` and `distinct_count`, empty `values`, no `rows_by_value` charts.

row_count.description: Rows the viewer can read, after the row filters of their data role; null when not counted yet or the count failed.

time_column.description: Time column of the time span and the time charts; null when the dataset has no time column.

time_start.description: First and last day with data in `time_column` (YYYY-MM-DD), among the rows the viewer can read.

label.description: First alias of the value; null when it has none.

rows.description: Rows holding this value, on every row of the version.

QueryFeedback.description: The stored rating of an answer.

approved.description:
An admin approved the answer as an example question: its question and SQL are now examples in the prompt of
later questions on the same dataset that share a word with it.

QuestionType.description:
Kind of question by the purpose of the analysis, as the classify step decided: `quantitative` (a number, a list or
a comparison, answered by one SQL query) or `causal` (why a number changed or differs between two groups, answered by
a breakdown).

Rating.description: `good` is the button for a good answer, `bad` the one for an answer that falls short.

RelatedDataset.description: A dataset linked to this one by a foreign key of the source database.

direction.description: `many_to_one` when this dataset holds the foreign key, `one_to_many` when the related dataset holds it.

related_columns.description: Key columns of the related dataset, in the same order.

RelatedTable.description: A table linked to the chosen table by one foreign key.

addable.description: True when `table` can be snapshotted with the chosen table and the relation recorded.

column_count.description: Readable columns of `table`; 0 when the account cannot read it.

from_table.description: Table holding the foreign key (the many side) and its key columns.

reason.description: Why the table cannot be added, in Vietnamese; null when addable.

table.description: `schema.table` that can be snapshotted together with the chosen table.

to_table.description: Table the foreign key points to (the one side) and its key columns.

column_count.description: Readable columns of the chosen table.

many_to_one.description: Tables the chosen table points to (its foreign keys).

one_to_many.description: Tables pointing to the chosen table (their foreign keys).

ReorderReportRequest.description: Every item id of the report, in the new order.

ReportBreakdown.description:
The breakdown kept with an item: the change between two periods or two groups and the groups of its first dimension
that made most of it. Numbers are decimal strings as in `Explanation`.

dimension.description: Label of the dimension the groups belong to.

name.description: Group value as text; empty for a missing value.

share_of_change.description: Share of the total change, decimal string; null when the change is zero.

ReportFacts.description:
Facts the backend computed from the numbers of the item when it was rendered (no language model): the main finding
and its points, Vietnamese.

ReportItem.description:
One item of a report, rendered again: the stored question and answer, and the result of running its stored SQL
again through the guard with the caller's access, on the data versions the question read.

oneOf.description:
The answer text shown when the question was asked, with its checks. Null when it was not stored, or when the
caller may now see fewer rows than when the question was asked (the stored text could cite rows outside them).

error.description: Vietnamese message when the stored SQL could not run again; the other result fields are then null.

oneOf.description: Facts computed again from `result`; null when the result shape has none.

Meaning check of `answer` (a separate model call compared the text with the computed facts); null when it did
not run or `answer` is null.

notes.description:
Vietnamese notes on how this rendering differs from when the question was asked (row count, newer table
version, fewer visible rows).

oneOf.description: Number check of `answer`; null when `answer` is null.
Result rows, at most as many as an answer sends; `total_rows` is the full count.

sql.description: SQL that ran now, after the guard.

tables.description: Tables and versions the question read, the starting table first.

oneOf.description: How the numbers were computed: measures, filters (including the caller's row filters), grouping, period.

ReportKind.description: `manual`: answers the user added one by one; `automatic`: built by the backend for one dataset.

ReportListResponse.description: Reports of the caller, last changed first.

ReportResponse.description: A report with every item rendered again from the stored questions.

rendered_at.description: When the items were run again; numbers of every item are as of this time, on the stored data versions.

ReportSummary.description: One report of the caller, without its items.

dataset_id.description: Dataset of an automatic report (`DatasetSummary.id`); null for a manual report.

intro.description: Opening paragraph written by the owner (Vietnamese); empty when none.

model_calls.description: Language model calls made while building an automatic report; null for a manual report.

ReportTableVersion.description: Table and data version an item read.

captured_at.description: When this version was snapshotted or uploaded.

is_current.description: False when the table has a newer version: the item still reads this one.

temporary_password.description: Shown once to hand to the user; not stored anywhere in plain text.

name.description:
Column name as the SQL returns it, made unique: from left to right, a name already used gets the smallest
suffix `_2`, `_3`, ... that no column has, so `a, a, a_2` becomes `a, a_3, a_2`.

ResultTable.description: Rows of the result; null in `AskResponse` unless the status is `answered`. At most 1000 rows are sent.

limit_reached.description:
True when `total_rows` equals the guard's row cap (whether the guard added the LIMIT or lowered one the SQL
had): the full result may have more rows, so show
`total_rows` as "at least".

rows.description: One array per row, cells in the order of `columns`; null is a SQL NULL.

total_rows.description: Number of rows `sql_guarded` returned. This is the full result unless `limit_reached`.

truncated.description: True when `rows` holds fewer rows than `total_rows`.

RolePolicy.description:
A row rule of a data role: members with this role see only the rows of table `table_id` whose `column` is one of
`allowed_values`.

allowed_values.description: Values of `column` the role sees; empty means no rows of the table.

column.description: A dimension column of the table.

SanityCheck.description: A plausibility rule for values of the concept. `min` and `max` only with `value_range`, at least one of them.

SanityCheckKind.description: `value_range`: the value lies in [min, max], one end may be missing. `non_negative`: the value is not negative.

SavedAnswer.description:
The answer text of a recorded question, as shown when it was asked: `answer_text` of a plain question, or
`explanation.summary` of a "why" question. Result rows are not stored.

by_model.description: True when a language model wrote the text and it passed the checks; false when the backend wrote it.

text.description: Vietnamese text for the end user.

oneOf.description:
Verdict of the independent model call that compared the meaning of the model's text with the computed facts
(`match`, `warning`, `mismatch`); null when the check did not run.

warnings.description: Points the check found unclear in the model's text; empty when `by_model` is false.

SetPoliciesRequest.description: The full rule set of a role; replaces the previous one.

policies.description: One rule per table and column. Each `column` must be a dimension column of the table's current version.
Rules as saved: values trimmed, without duplicates, sorted.

warnings.description: Vietnamese notes for the admin, for example a value not found in the column profile. The rules are saved.

setup_code.description: Code printed in the backend log at startup; case and surrounding spaces are ignored.

workspace_name.description: Name of the first workspace; empty gives a default name.

needed.description: True while the installation has no account yet: show the first-run setup screen instead of sign-in.

SheetSummary.description: A sheet of an Excel file, as shown when choosing sheets to upload.

approx_rows.description:
Rows below the header, from the data range the file records. An estimate: may include empty rows, 0 when the
file does not record it.

columns.description: Column names from the header row, normalised as on upload; empty if the sheet has no data.

hidden.description: Hidden in Excel. Hidden sheets are skipped when no sheet is chosen.

SkipCause.description: Why a table keeps metadata only.

SliceName.description: `base` or `compare`: one of the two slices of `AskResponse.explanation`.

dataset_id.description:
Snapshot this table (a `datasets.id`, the field name predates tables) again, with every table of the same source
linked to it by relations.

name.description: Name stored for `table` when it is new; defaults to the table name. Other tables use their table name.

table.description:
`schema.table` named `name` when it is new. Optional: without `table`, `tables` and `dataset_id`, every table
and view the account can read is snapshotted.

tables.description:
`schema.table` names to snapshot (the ticked tables), each stored as one table of the database dataset. Empty
with no `table` and no `dataset_id`: every readable table. One name snapshots that one table, for example a table kept as metadata
only. Not allowed with `dataset_id`.

datasets.description: One entry per table copied. `created` is false for a table whose content did not change.

metadata_only.description:
Tables over SOURCE_TABLE_MAX_MB, the SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_MAX_MB total, or SOURCE_MAX_ROWS when set: no rows copied,
metadata kept.

relations.description: Foreign-key relations recorded for these datasets (both ends snapshotted from this source).

unreadable.description:
Tables this source held that the account can no longer read (re-snapshot only); their datasets keep their
last version.

SourceResponse.description: A database source without its password.

custom_ca.description: True when the source was added with its own CA certificate.

SourceTableInfo.description: A table or view the source account can read, with what the connect screen needs to pick tables.

comment.description: `COMMENT ON TABLE`, cleaned; null when none.

dataset_id.description: Dataset of the table when `state` is `snapshotted`.

estimated_rows.description: Row estimate from Postgres statistics (last ANALYZE); null when Postgres has none yet, and for views.

is_referenced.description:
True when another readable table points to this one (a lookup table): unticking it leaves those tables without
the relation.

oneOf.description:
Limit this table alone is over, from Postgres statistics: `size_limit` above SOURCE_TABLE_MAX_MB, `row_limit`
above SOURCE_MAX_ROWS when set. A snapshot keeps its metadata only. Null when it fits (the SOURCE_SNAPSHOT_MAX_MB
total depends on the other ticked tables and is not checked here).

reason.description: Why the table has metadata only; null otherwise.

referenced_by.description: Foreign keys of other readable tables pointing to this table.

references.description: Foreign keys of this table pointing to other readable tables.

size_bytes.description: Size reported by Postgres (`pg_table_size`, without indexes); null for views.

oneOf.description: What this source already holds for the table; null when never snapshotted.

StepName.description:
Step of the backend:
- `context`: read the dataset profile and build the prompt.
- `classify`: the language model tells a plain question from a question that asks for a cause; when the model
  fails, the keyword rule decides and the step is not ok.
- `llm`: the language model writes SQL.
- `guard`: check the SQL, add row-level filters and a row limit.
- `run`: run the SQL on the analytics engine.
- `repair`: the language model fixes SQL that failed to run, or that the guard refused because a table or column
  does not exist or because it could build a value too large (at most once).
- `explain`: compute the breakdown of a "why" question (code, no model).
- `narrate`: the language model writes the summary of the breakdown, or the `insight.summary` of a plain question
  (also used as its `answer_text`).
- `record`: save the question in the history.

SummaryPoint.description: One point of the summary: a short lead (shown in bold) and the sentence after it.

lead.description: Lead of the point (Vietnamese), for example "Lý do chính".

SummaryPointKind.description:
- `reason`: what mostly makes the change (the volume and the value per unit, or the mix and the rate); every point
  written by the model has this kind.
- `outliers`: groups that changed much more or much less than the whole, or exist on one side only.
- `even`: no group stands out; the largest contributions are the largest groups.
- `largest`: the group with the largest contribution in the direction of the change, when the numbers do not allow
  comparing groups with the whole (a base slice of zero or less, or a change too close to zero).
- `against`: a group that moved the other way.
- `dropped`: dimensions the summary leaves out and why; they stay in `Explanation.dimensions`.

TableColumn.description: A column of the current version of a table.

aliases.description: Other names of the column (semantic profile), used to match question words.

description_source.description: `database` (comment in the source database) or `model` (written by the semantic profile); null when unknown.

is_sensitive.description: Sensitive column: its values never go to the language model.

TableLink.description: A foreign key between two readable tables, as declared in the source database.

from_table.description: Table holding the foreign key (the many side) and its key columns.

to_table.description: Table the foreign key points to (the one side) and its key columns.

TableRead.description: A dataset the SQL of an answer read.

logical_table.description: Table name the SQL uses for this dataset.

name.description: Dataset name as shown in the dataset list.

TableState.description: What a source holds for one table.

table_count.description: Number of tables and views the account can read.

TimeGrain.description: Period of the time charts: by day when the data spans at most 92 days, else by month.

TurnItem.description: One recorded question of a conversation. Questions waiting for a choice (`needs_choice`) are not recorded.

oneOf.description:
The answer text shown when the question was asked; null unless answered, and for questions recorded before
answers were stored.
The rating the caller gave this answer; null when not rated.

query_id.description: Id of the question in the history; use it to trace source rows like a single question.

sql.description: SQL that ran (`sql_guarded`); null when the guard refused it.

understood.description: Short text of the "understood as" card (measures, filters, grouping, period); null unless answered.

Understanding.description:
The "understood as" card, built from `sql_guarded`: what is measured, filtered, grouped, sorted, over which
period, and the assumptions made. Null in `AskResponse` unless the status is `answered`. `limit` is null when only
the guard's row cap applies; `time_range` is null when the SQL has no time filter.

assumptions.description: Assumptions the user can change, including clarifications answered earlier; every entry has `selected` set.

filters.description:
Filters of the question, then the row-level filters the guard added for the user's data role (the label says
which).

oneOf.description: Row limit the question asked for, for example the top 3; null when only the guard's limit applies.
Period the question covers; null when the SQL has no time filter.

UnderstoodItem.description: One thing the question was understood to mean.

from_previous.description:
True when the item is carried over from the previous turn of the conversation: the same as in that turn's card
(same SQL fragment or same label) and not named in this question. Omitted when false.

label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese) naming the measure, filter, grouping, order or period.

sql.description: Fragment of `sql_guarded` this item comes from.

UpdateReportRequest.description: Fields left out keep their value.

UploadDatasetRequest.description: Multipart form for uploading a dataset. Total size is limited by MAX_UPLOAD_MB (413 above it).

dataset_id.description: Add a new version to this dataset instead of creating a new one.

file.description:
One or more CSV or Parquet files (repeat the field), or one Excel `.xlsx` file. Files with the same columns are
stacked into one table.

name.description: Name of the new dataset; defaults to the first file name.

sheet.description:
Sheet of the Excel file to upload; repeat to stack several sheets with the same columns. Not needed when the
file has one sheet.

columns.description: Columns of the new table; empty when `created` is false.

created.description: False when the files match an existing version: nothing new was created.

UserSummary.description: An account in the system administrator's list.

ValueKind.description:
How to read the cells of a column, decided by the column type. Any cell may also be null (SQL NULL).
- `text`: JSON string.
- `number`: JSON number, for types a JavaScript number holds exactly: integers up to 32 bits, FLOAT, DOUBLE. NaN
  and infinity are sent as null.
- `decimal`: JSON string of decimal digits, integer or not, for example "5000" or "-1234.50", for BIGINT
  (COUNT returns one), HUGEINT, unsigned 64 and 128 bit integers and DECIMAL, which a JavaScript number would
  round. Convert with `Number()` only to draw a chart or to sort; comparing the strings sorts "10" before "9".
- `boolean`: JSON boolean.
- `date`: JSON string `YYYY-MM-DD`.
- `timestamp`: JSON string in ISO 8601, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.ffffff]` for TIMESTAMP (no time zone, as stored),
  ending in `Z` for TIMESTAMPTZ (converted to UTC).
- `other`: JSON string as the analytics engine prints the value: TIME, INTERVAL, lists, structs and other types.

A `date` or `timestamp` with a year after 9999 or before 1 AD uses the ISO 8601 expanded form: `+10000-01-01`;
year 1 BC is `0000`, 2 BC is `-0001`. Infinite dates and times are sent as null. A result column of type TIME_NS,
TIME WITH TIME ZONE, BIT, BIGNUM, VARIANT, GEOMETRY or a type the backend does not recognize is not read: the `run`
step fails and the fix round casts it to text.

llm.description: Language model provider in use, for example `mock` or `gemini-2.5-flash`.

VolumePrice.description:
Change split into a volume effect and a price effect, for a measure that is volume times price (for example
orders times average order value); null in `Explanation` for other measures.

base_price.description: Measure divided by volume, rounded to a fixed number of decimals; the only rounded numbers here.

if_volume_unchanged.description: Value of the measure if the volume had stayed at `base_volume`: `base_volume * compare_price`.

price_effect.description: `change - volume_effect`, so that the two effects add up to `change` exactly.

price_label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese) naming the price, for example the average order value.

sql.description: SQL that computed the volume and the measure of both slices, after the guard.

volume_effect.description: `(compare_volume - base_volume) * (base_price + compare_price) / 2`, exact from the rounded prices.

volume_label.description: Text for the end user (Vietnamese) naming the volume, for example the number of orders.

WarningCode.description:
Kind of note:
- `empty_result`: no rows.
- `all_null`: a result column holds only nulls.
- `filter_value_not_found`: the SQL filters on a value that does not occur in the column.
- `unusual_magnitude`: a value is far outside what the data makes likely, for example a ratio above 100%.
- `explanation_unavailable`: a "why" question was answered without a breakdown; the message says why.
- `choice_not_applied`: a choice sent with the question was not recognized and the default was used.
- `premise_mismatch`: a "why" question assumes a direction (a drop, a rise) that the computed change does not have;
  the breakdown explains the actual change.

WorkspaceOverview.description: A workspace as the system administrator sees it: name and members, none of its data.
